newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on moderate volumes.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed on moderate volumes Tuesday, holding above Monday's intraday lows, with the exception of palladium which saw fresh life-of-contract lows.

"Gold and silver look oversold after 10 days of falls and we may see a bounce back above $385.00 basis spot, where it's likely we may see some producer selling to lock in the contango, in case gold tests support around $380 again," Mitsui & Co USA bullion dealer, Greg Drury said.
"But there may be some producer buybacks from Australian miners down around $381 which could provide support."
COMEX December gold ended down 40 cents at $386.80 an ounce, after finding support at the session lows at $386.00.

In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted $383.00/383.40 at the close, compared to the London afternoon fix at $383.10. Earlier gold had fixed at a fresh two month low of $382.45 in London. New York bullion was quoted $383.40/383.80 a the close Monday.
Open interest in the COMEX December contract rose 11,809 lots Monday, suggesting the high total volume in gold futures of 59,000 lots may have included new short positions," analysts said.
December silver ended up 1.5 cents at $5.143 an ounce, after trading in a $5.105-$5.150 range.
Open interest in December silver has risen steadily to 308,904,000 ounces as of September 9, compared to COMEX warehouse stocks of 151,666,387 ounces.
Both gold and silver have drifted lower for ten days now, on fund selling and weak physical demand by fabricators and investors, suggesting the July/August rally may have ended, analysts said.
NYMEX October platinum ended up 20 cents at $395.80 an ounce, while NYMEX December palladium ended $2.10 an ounce at $123.85, after seeing a new contract low at $122.00.
News from the world auto industry remains mixed for platinum group metals demand for emissions catalysts, CPM Group analysts said.
U.S. car and light truck sales slipped 2.3 percent in August to 1,306,159 vehicles, though sales for the first eight months of the year are up 3.8 pct from the same period last year.
New car registrations in Europe in August stood at 479,407, up 2.2 percent on August last year, but the pace of growth looked to be slowing.

Japanese auto sales slipped to 290,144 in August, down 2.1 pct from the same period last year, though sales were up 1.5 pct at 4.24 million units in the first seven months of 1996, compared to the same period last year.
